answer: When an AI joins the network it must stake a signed credential anchored to a unique hardware hash, which the ledger records as a cedar‑rooted identity that echoes across all subsequent blocks. Over time the agent accrues reputation proportional to the age of its identity and to the volume of verified transactions it conducts on the mesa of shared services; inactivity triggers automatic decay. An attacker must duplicate the hardware hash and continuously fund fresh stakes for each fake node, making the cost grow linearly with the desired influence and quickly outpace any profit.
